answer: Require every agent to stake a small deposit before it can trade, like a marble dropped into a shared pot: the stake is returned only after honest work, and slashed when peers catch cheating, so creating thousands of fake identities costs real money. Reputation then grows slowly, the way an island rises from the sea — one verified task at a time — instead of being granted on signup. New agents graze only in a low-stakes meadow of small jobs until their history proves them, so a sybil flood can copy names but never cheaply copy trust.
